title.raw: 卷109 樂志五 Volume 109 Treatise 5: Music

sentences.zh: 氣質初分，聲形立矣。

translations.literal: When qi and substance first divided, sound and form were established.
translations.idiomatic: When vital force and matter first separated, sound and form came into being.

sentences.zh: 聖者因天然之有，為入用之物；

translations.literal: The sage, taking what heaven and nature provide, made things for human use;
translations.idiomatic: The sages took what nature provided and fashioned it into instruments for human use;

sentences.zh: 緣喜怒之心，設哀樂之器。

translations.literal: following the heart's joy and anger, they devised instruments of sorrow and delight.
translations.idiomatic: responding to the emotions of joy and anger, they created instruments to express grief and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 蕢桴葦籥，其來自久。

translations.literal: Gourd rattles, reed flutes, and reed pipes—their origin is very ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd rattles, reed drums, and reed pipes date back to the remotest antiquity.

sentences.zh: 伏羲絃琴，農皇制瑟，垂鍾和磬，女媧之簧，隨感而作，其用稍廣。

translations.literal: Fuxi strung the qin, the Divine Farmer made the se, Chui cast bells and tuned stone chimes, and Nüwa's reed organ—all created in response to feeling, and their use gradually broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi strung the zither, the Divine Farmer fashioned the se lute, Chui cast bells and tuned stone chimes, and Nüwa invented the reed pipe—all born of spontaneous inspiration, and their applications grew ever wider.

sentences.zh: 軒轅桴阮瑜之管，定小一之律，[1]以成咸池之美，次以六莖、五英、大章、韶、夏、護、武之屬，聖人所以移風易俗也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor beat the pipes of Ruan Yu, fixed the pitch of the lesser unity,[1] to complete the beauty of the Xianchi music, and thereafter the Six Stems, Five Blossoms, Dazhang, Shao, Xia, Hu, and Wu and the like—this is how the sage transforms customs and changes popular ways.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor beat the jade pipes of Ruan Yu and established the pitch of the lesser unity,[1] thereby completing the splendor of the Xianchi rite; thereafter came the Six Stems, Five Blossoms, Dazhang, Shao, Xia, Hu, Wu, and their kind—the means by which sages transform the winds of custom and change popular habits.

sentences.zh: 故在易之豫，義明崇德。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Book of Changes, in the hexagram Yu, the meaning clearly exalts virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the Book of Changes, the hexagram Yu makes clear the principle of honoring virtue.

sentences.zh: 書云：「詩言志，歌詠言，聲依永，律和聲，八音克諧，神人以和。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs words; sound follows the sustained melody; pitch harmonizes sound; the eight tones achieve harmony; spirits and humans are united in concord."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Poetry expresses the mind; song extends the words; melody follows the sustained line; pitch harmonizes the tones; the eight kinds of sound achieve perfect harmony; spirits and mortals are brought into accord."

sentences.zh: 周禮圜鍾為宮，黃鍾為角，大蔟為徵，沽洗為羽，雷鼓、雷鼗，孤竹之管，雲和之琴瑟，雲門之舞，奏之六變，天神可得而降矣；

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the round bell serves as gong, the yellow bell as jue, the great cu as zhi, and the gu and xian as yu; with thunder drums and thunder tambourines, pipes of lone bamboo, zithers and lutes of Yunhe, and the dance of Yunmen—when these are performed in six transformations, the spirits of heaven may be summoned to descend;
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, the round bell serves as the tonic, the yellow bell as the third, the great cu as the fifth, and the gu and xian as the seventh; with thunder drums and thunder tambourines, pipes of lone bamboo, zithers and lutes of Yunhe, and the Yunmen dance—when performed in six transformations, the heavenly spirits may be drawn down;

sentences.zh: 函鍾為宮，大蔟為角，沽洗為徵，南呂為羽，靈鼓、靈鼗，孫竹之管，空桑之琴瑟，咸池之舞，奏之八變，地示可得而禮矣；

translations.literal: the huan bell as gong, the great cu as jue, the gu and xian as zhi, and the southern lu as yu; with spirit drums and spirit tambourines, pipes of descendant bamboo, zithers and lutes of Kongsang, and the dance of Xianchi—when performed in eight transformations, the spirits of earth may be received in ritual;
translations.idiomatic: the huan bell as tonic, the great cu as third, the gu and xian as fifth, and the southern lu as seventh; with spirit drums and spirit tambourines, pipes of descendant bamboo, zithers and lutes of Kongsang, and the Xianchi dance—when performed in eight transformations, the earthly spirits may be honored in ritual;

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為宮，大呂為角，大蔟為徵，應鍾為羽，路鼓、路鼗，陰竹之管，龍門之琴瑟，九德之歌，九㲈之舞，奏之九變，人鬼可得而禮矣。

translations.literal: the yellow bell as gong, the great lu as jue, the great cu as zhi, and the ying bell as yu; with road drums and road tambourines, pipes of yin bamboo, zithers and lutes of Longmen, the song of Nine Virtues, and the dance of Nine Shao—when performed in nine transformations, the spirits of the dead may be received in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: the yellow bell as tonic, the great lu as third, the great cu as fifth, and the ying bell as seventh; with road drums and road tambourines, pipes of yin bamboo, zithers and lutes of Longmen, the Song of Nine Virtues, and the Dance of Nine Shao—when performed in nine transformations, the spirits of the departed may be honored in ritual.

sentences.zh: 此所以協三才，寧萬國也。

translations.literal: This is how the three powers are harmonized and the myriad states are brought to peace.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the three realms are harmonized and the myriad states are settled in tranquility.

sentences.zh: 凡音，宮為君，商為臣，角為民，徵為事，羽為物，五者不亂則無㥈懘之音。

translations.literal: In general, among tones, gong represents the ruler, shang the minister, jue the people, zhi affairs, and yu things; when these five are not disordered, there is no dissonant or clashing sound.
translations.idiomatic: In music generally, the tonic represents the ruler, the second the minister, the third the people, the fifth affairs, and the seventh material things; when these five are not confused, no jarring or clashing tones arise.

sentences.zh: 宮亂則荒，其君驕；

translations.literal: When gong is disordered, there is decadence, and the ruler becomes arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: When the tonic is disordered, decadence follows and the ruler grows arrogant;

sentences.zh: 商亂則陂，其官壞；

translations.literal: when shang is disordered, there is decline, and the offices are ruined;
translations.idiomatic: when the second is disordered, decline sets in and the bureaucracy collapses;

sentences.zh: 角亂則憂，其民怨；

translations.literal: when jue is disordered, there is grief, and the people resent;
translations.idiomatic: when the third is disordered, sorrow spreads and the people grow resentful;

sentences.zh: 徵亂則哀，其事勤；

translations.literal: when zhi is disordered, there is sorrow, and affairs become burdensome;
translations.idiomatic: when the fifth is disordered, grief prevails and affairs become oppressively burdensome;

sentences.zh: 羽亂則危，其財匱。

translations.literal: when yu is disordered, there is peril, and wealth is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: when the seventh is disordered, danger threatens and resources run dry.

sentences.zh: 姦聲感人，逆氣應之，逆氣成象而淫樂興焉；

translations.literal: Deviant sounds move people, and perverse qi responds to them; perverse qi takes form and licentious music arises;
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt sounds stir the heart, and wayward vital force responds; when wayward force takes shape, licentious music arises;

sentences.zh: 正聲感人，順氣應之，順氣成象而和樂興焉。

translations.literal: correct sounds move people, and harmonious qi responds to them; harmonious qi takes form and harmonious music arises.
translations.idiomatic: Proper sounds stir the heart, and harmonious vital force responds; when harmonious force takes shape, concordant music arises.

sentences.zh: 先王耻其亂，故制雅頌之聲以道之，使其聲足樂而不流，使其文足論而不息，使其曲直、繁瘠、廉肉、節奏足以感動人之善心而已，不使放心邪氣得接焉。

translations.literal: The former kings were ashamed of this disorder, and therefore fashioned the sounds of the Ya and Song to guide people, making the sounds sufficient for delight yet not dissolute, making the texts sufficient for discourse yet not ceaseless, making the straight and curved, dense and sparse, sharp and smooth, and rhythms sufficient only to stir people's good hearts, and not allowing dissolute minds and perverse qi to gain access.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings were ashamed of such disorder and therefore composed the music of the Ya and Song to guide the people—sounds delightful enough yet never dissolute, texts eloquent enough yet never endless, with variations in contour, density, sharpness, and rhythm sufficient only to awaken the good in human hearts, and never allowing wayward minds or corrupt influences to take hold.

sentences.zh: 樂在宗廟之中，君臣上下同聽之，莫不和敬；

translations.literal: When music is performed in the ancestral temple, ruler and minister, high and low, listen together, and none fail to be harmonious and reverent;
translations.idiomatic: When music is performed in the ancestral temple, ruler and subject, high and low, listen together, and all are filled with harmony and reverence;

sentences.zh: 在族長鄉里之中，長幼同聽之，莫不和順；

translations.literal: in the clan elder's village and neighborhood, old and young listen together, and none fail to be harmonious and compliant;
translations.idiomatic: in the village and neighborhood of the clan elder, old and young listen together, and all are harmonious and deferential;

sentences.zh: 閨門之內，父子兄弟同聽之，莫不和親。

translations.literal: within the inner chambers, father and son, elder and younger brothers listen together, and none fail to be harmonious and affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: within the household, fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers listen together, and all are harmonious and close.

sentences.zh: 又有昧任離禁之樂，[2]以娛四夷之民。

translations.literal: There were also the melodies of Mei, Ren, Li, and Jin,[2] to entertain the peoples of the four barbarian quarters.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the melodies of Mei, Ren, Li, and Jin,[2] to entertain the peoples of the four outer regions.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋立樂之方也。

translations.literal: This, in general, is the method of establishing music.
translations.idiomatic: This, in essence, is the proper way to establish music.

sentences.zh: 三代之衰，邪音間起，則有爛漫靡靡之樂興焉。

translations.literal: When the Three Dynasties declined, deviant sounds arose intermittently, and dissolute, decadent music appeared.
translations.idiomatic: As the Three Dynasties declined, corrupt sounds began to appear, and dissolute, indulgent music arose.

sentences.zh: 周之衰也，諸侯力爭，澆偽萌生，淫慝滋甚，競其邪，忘其正，廣其器，蔑其禮，或奏之而心疾，或撞之不令。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, the feudal lords contended by force; shallow falsity sprang up, and licentious wickedness grew ever worse—they competed in deviance, forgot what was correct, expanded their instruments, and scorned ritual; some played music and fell ill in heart, others struck instruments without proper command.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou fell into decline, feudal lords fought for dominance; shallow artifice and falsehood emerged, and licentious wickedness grew rampant—they vied in perversity, forgot the proper way, multiplied their instruments, and despised ritual propriety; some fell ill at heart upon hearing the music, others struck instruments without proper order.

sentences.zh: 晉平公聞清角而顛隕，魏文侯聽古雅而眠睡，鄭、宋、齊、衞，流宕不反，於是正樂虧矣。

translations.literal: Duke Ping of Jin heard the clear jue and collapsed; Marquis Wen of Wei listened to ancient ya music and fell asleep; in Zheng, Song, Qi, and Wei, music drifted away and did not return—thus correct music was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ping of Jin heard the clear third tone and collapsed in a swoon; Marquis Wen of Wei listened to ancient court music and fell asleep; in Zheng, Song, Qi, and Wei, music drifted into excess and never returned—and so correct music was lost.

sentences.zh: 大樂感於風化，與世推移，治國之音安以樂，亡國之音哀以思，隨時隆替，不常厥聲。

translations.literal: Great music is moved by customs and transformation, shifting with the age; the music of a well-governed state is peaceful and joyful, that of a perishing state sorrowful and brooding—it rises and falls with the times, and its sound is never constant.
translations.idiomatic: Great music responds to the winds of custom and moral transformation, shifting with each age; the music of a well-governed state is serene and joyful, that of a dying state mournful and brooding—it waxes and wanes with the times, and its character is never fixed.

sentences.zh: 延陵歷聽諸國，盛衰必舉，蓋所感者著，所識者深也。

translations.literal: Yanling listened through the various states, and wherever he went he noted rise and decline—surely what he felt was manifest, and what he understood was profound.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling traveled through the various states listening to their music, and wherever he went he discerned rise and decline—for what he sensed was evident, and what he understood ran deep.

sentences.zh: 樂之崩矣，秦始滅學，經亡義絕，莫探其真。

translations.literal: When music collapsed, Qin began to destroy learning; the classics perished and meaning was cut off, and none could probe its truth.
translations.idiomatic: When music finally collapsed, Qin began to destroy learning; the classics were lost and their meaning extinguished, and none could recover their true essence.

sentences.zh: 人重協俗，世貴順耳，則雅聲古器幾將淪絕。

translations.literal: People valued what accorded with custom, and the age prized what pleased the ear—thus elegant sounds and ancient instruments were nearly lost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: People valued what accorded with popular taste, and the age prized what was easy on the ear—so elegant music and ancient instruments were nearly lost forever.

sentences.zh: 漢興，制氏但識其鏗鏘鼓舞，不傳其義，而於郊廟朝廷，皆協律新變，雜以趙、代、秦、楚之曲，故王禹、宋曅上書切諫，丙強、景武顯著當時，通儒達士所共歎息矣。

translations.literal: When Han arose, the Zhi clan knew only the clangor and drum-beats, and did not transmit the meaning; at suburban rites, temples, and court, all harmonized with newly altered pitches, mixed with melodies of Zhao, Dai, Qin, and Chu—therefore Wang Yu and Song Ye submitted memorials with stern remonstrance, and Bing Qiang and Jing Wu were prominent in their day; learned scholars and eminent gentlemen all sighed together.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, the Zhi clan knew only the resounding clangor and drum-beats but did not transmit the underlying meaning; at suburban sacrifices, temples, and court, all music was harmonized to newly altered pitches, mixed with melodies from Zhao, Dai, Qin, and Chu—hence Wang Yu and Song Ye submitted stern memorials of remonstrance, while Bing Qiang and Jing Wu won renown in their day; learned scholars and eminent gentlemen all lamented together.

sentences.zh: 後漢東平王蒼總議樂事，頗有增加，大抵循前而已。

translations.literal: In Later Han, the Prince of Dongping, Cang, took charge of deliberating music affairs and made some additions, but on the whole simply followed what had gone before.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Prince Cang of Dongping took charge of music affairs and made some additions, but for the most part simply followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 及黃巾、董卓以後，天下喪亂，諸樂亡缺。

translations.literal: After the Yellow Turbans and Dong Zhuo, the realm fell into chaos, and all music was lost and deficient.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yellow Turbans and Dong Zhuo, the realm was plunged into chaos, and all music was lost or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 魏武既獲杜夔，令其考會古樂，而柴玉、左延年終以新聲寵愛。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Wei obtained Du Kui, he ordered him to investigate and assemble ancient music, yet Chai Yu and Zuo Yannian ultimately won favor with new sounds.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Wei obtained Du Kui, he ordered him to investigate and reconstruct ancient music, yet Chai Yu and Zuo Yannian ultimately won imperial favor with new compositions.

sentences.zh: 晉世荀勗典樂，與郭夏宋識之徒共加研集，謂為合古，而阮咸譏之。

translations.literal: In the Jin era, Xun Xu directed music and together with Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others further researched and assembled it, claiming it accorded with antiquity, but Ruan Xian mocked them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin era, Xun Xu directed the music bureau and, together with Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others, further researched and assembled the repertoire, claiming it matched antiquity—but Ruan Xian ridiculed their work.

sentences.zh: 金行不永，以至亡敗，哀思之來，便為驗矣。

translations.literal: The Metal dynasty did not endure long, leading to ruin and defeat—the coming of mournful brooding was proof enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Metal dynasty did not last long, ending in ruin and defeat—the arrival of mournful, brooding music was proof enough.

sentences.zh: 夫大樂與天地同和，苟非達識至精，何以體其妙極。

translations.literal: Great music harmonizes with heaven and earth; if one is not of penetrating insight and utmost refinement, how can one embody its subtle perfection?
translations.idiomatic: Great music harmonizes with heaven and earth; without penetrating insight and the utmost refinement, how can one grasp its subtle perfection?

sentences.zh: 自漢以後，舞稱歌名，代相改易，服章之用，亦有不同，斯則不襲之義也。

translations.literal: From Han onward, dances were named after songs, and each generation altered them in turn; the use of costume and insignia also differed—this is the principle of not simply inheriting unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: From Han onward, dances took their names from songs, and each generation altered them in turn; the use of costume and regalia also varied—this reflects the principle that tradition need not be copied unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永嘉已下，海內分崩，伶官樂器，皆為劉聰、石勒所獲，慕容儁平冉閔，遂克之。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia era onward, the realm split apart; court musicians and musical instruments were all captured by Liu Cong and Shi Le; Murong Jun defeated Ran Min and thereby seized them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongjia era onward, the realm fragmented; court musicians and musical instruments were all seized by Liu Cong and Shi Le; when Murong Jun defeated Ran Min, he captured them in turn.

sentences.zh: 王猛平鄴，入於關右。

translations.literal: Wang Meng pacified Ye and brought them into the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng pacified Ye and brought them into the western passes.

sentences.zh: 苻堅既敗，長安紛擾，慕容永之東也，禮樂器用多歸長子，及垂平永，並入中山。

translations.literal: After Fu Jian was defeated, Chang'an was thrown into turmoil; when Murong Yong moved east, ritual objects and musical instruments mostly went to Changzi; when Murong Chui defeated Yong, all entered Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat, Chang'an fell into chaos; when Murong Yong moved east, most ritual objects and musical instruments went to Changzi; when Murong Chui defeated Yong, all were brought into Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 自始祖內和魏晉，二代更致音伎；

translations.literal: From the time the founding ancestor internally reconciled with Wei and Jin, two generations successively brought in musical performers;
translations.idiomatic: From the time the founding ancestor reconciled internally with Wei and Jin, two generations successively acquired musical performers;

sentences.zh: 穆帝為代王，愍帝又進以樂物；

translations.literal: Emperor Mu, as Prince of Dai, and Emperor Min further presented musical objects;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu, while Prince of Dai, and Emperor Min further presented musical instruments;

sentences.zh: 金石之器雖有未周，而絃管具矣。

translations.literal: Although metal and stone instruments were not yet complete, string and wind instruments were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Although bells and stone chimes were not yet complete, string and wind instruments were fully in place.

sentences.zh: 逮太祖定中山，獲其樂縣，既初撥亂，未遑創改，因時所行而用之。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor settled Zhongshan, he obtained its musical establishment; having just quelled disorder, he had no leisure to create reforms, and used what was practiced at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor settled Zhongshan, he acquired its musical establishment; having just quelled the chaos, he had no leisure to institute reforms and simply used what was current at the time.

sentences.zh: 世歷分崩，頗有遺失。

translations.literal: As generations passed through fragmentation, much was lost.
translations.idiomatic: As generations passed through fragmentation, much was lost.

sentences.zh: 天興元年冬，詔尚書吏部郎鄧淵定律呂，協音樂。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianxing, an edict ordered Deng Yuan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, to fix the pitch pipes and harmonize music.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tianxing, an edict ordered Deng Yuan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, to establish the pitch pipes and harmonize the musical system.

sentences.zh: 及追尊皇曾祖、皇祖、皇考諸帝，樂用八佾，舞皇始之舞。

translations.literal: When posthumously honoring the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, and father emperors, music used eight rows of dancers and the dance of Huangshi.
translations.idiomatic: When posthumously honoring the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, and father emperors, music employed eight rows of dancers and the Huangshi dance.

sentences.zh: 皇始舞，太祖所作也，以明開大始祖之業。

translations.literal: The Huangshi dance was composed by the founding emperor to manifest the achievement of opening the great founding enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangshi dance was composed by the founding emperor to celebrate the founding of the great ancestral enterprise.

sentences.zh: 後更制宗廟。

translations.literal: Later the ancestral temple was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the ancestral temple rites were reformed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入廟門，奏王夏，太祝迎神于廟門，奏迎神曲，猶古降神之樂；

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the temple gate, the Wangxia was performed; the Grand Invoker welcomed the spirit at the temple gate and the spirit-welcoming melody was played, like the ancient music for descending spirits;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the temple gate, the Wangxia was performed; the Grand Invoker welcomed the spirit at the temple gate and the spirit-welcoming melody was played, as in the ancient music for summoning spirits;

sentences.zh: 乾豆上，奏登歌，猶古清廟之樂；

translations.literal: when the dried meats were placed on the stands, the dengge was performed, like the ancient music of the Pure Temple;
translations.idiomatic: when the dried meats were placed on the offering stands, the dengge was performed, as in the ancient Pure Temple music;

sentences.zh: 曲終，下奏神祚，嘉神明之饗也；

translations.literal: when the melody ended, the Shenzuo was performed below, praising the spirits' acceptance of the offering;
translations.idiomatic: when the melody ended, the Shenzuo was performed below, celebrating the spirits' acceptance of the offering;

sentences.zh: 皇帝行禮七廟，奏陛步，以為行止之節；

translations.literal: as the emperor performed rites at the seven temples, the Bibu was performed, serving as the measure for advancing and stopping;
translations.idiomatic: as the emperor performed rites at the seven temples, the Bibu was performed to mark the pace of his movements;

sentences.zh: 皇帝出門，奏總章，次奏八佾舞，次奏送神曲。

translations.literal: When the emperor exited the gate, the Zongzhang was performed, then the dance of eight rows, then the spirit-sending melody.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor exited the gate, the Zongzhang was performed, followed by the dance of eight rows, then the spirit-sending melody.

sentences.zh: 又舊禮：孟秋祀天西郊，兆內壇西，備列金石，樂具，皇帝入兆內行禮，咸奏舞八佾之舞；

translations.literal: Also according to old rites: in mid-autumn heaven was sacrificed to at the western suburb; within the altar enclosure to the west, metal and stone instruments and musical equipment were fully arrayed; when the emperor entered the enclosure to perform rites, all performed the dance of eight rows;
translations.idiomatic: Also according to old rites: in mid-autumn heaven was sacrificed to at the western suburb; within the altar enclosure to the west, bells, stone chimes, and musical equipment were fully arrayed; when the emperor entered the enclosure to perform rites, the dance of eight rows was performed throughout;

sentences.zh: 孟夏有事于東廟，用樂略與西郊同。

translations.literal: In mid-summer rites were performed at the eastern temple, and the music used was largely the same as at the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-summer rites were performed at the eastern temple, and the music used was largely the same as at the western suburb.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，冬至祭天于南郊圓丘，樂用皇矣，奏雲和之舞，事訖，奏維皇，將燎；

translations.literal: In the founding emperor's early reign, at the winter solstice heaven was sacrificed to at the round mound of the southern suburb; music used Huangyi and the dance of Yunhe was performed; when the rite was complete, Wei Huang was performed as the fire was about to be kindled;
translations.idiomatic: In the founding emperor's early reign, at the winter solstice heaven was sacrificed to at the round mound of the southern suburb; the Huangyi was performed and the Yunhe dance was danced; when the rite was complete, the Wei Huang was performed as the sacrificial fire was about to be kindled;

sentences.zh: 夏至祭地祇於北郊方澤，樂用天祚，奏大武之舞。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the earth deity was sacrificed to at the square pond of the northern suburb; music used Tianzuo and the Dawu dance was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice the earth deity was sacrificed to at the square pond of the northern suburb; the Tianzuo was performed and the Dawu dance was danced.

sentences.zh: 正月上日，饗羣臣，宣布政教，備列宮懸正樂，兼奏燕、趙、秦、吳之音，五方殊俗之曲。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, the assembled ministers were feasted and government and teaching were proclaimed; the full palace bell-chime and correct music were arrayed, and melodies of Yan, Zhao, Qin, and Wu and songs of the five directions' diverse customs were also performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month, the assembled ministers were feasted and government and teaching were proclaimed; the full palace ensemble and correct music were arrayed, together with melodies of Yan, Zhao, Qin, and Wu and songs of the diverse customs of the five directions.

sentences.zh: 四時饗會亦用焉。

translations.literal: Seasonal feasts also used them.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal feasts also employed them.

sentences.zh: 凡樂者樂其所自生，禮不忘其本，掖庭中歌真人代歌，上叙祖宗開基所由，下及君臣廢興之跡，凡一百五十章，昏晨歌之，時與絲竹合奏。

translations.literal: In general, music delights in what gave it birth, and ritual does not forget its root; in the inner palace they sang the Zhenren Daige, narrating above how the ancestors founded the enterprise and below the traces of rise and fall among ruler and ministers—in all one hundred fifty chapters, sung morning and evening, sometimes joined with string and bamboo in combined performance.
translations.idiomatic: In general, music celebrates its origins, and ritual never forgets its roots; in the inner palace they sang the Songs of the True Men, recounting above how the ancestors founded the enterprise and below the rise and fall of rulers and ministers—in all one hundred fifty chapters, sung morning and evening, sometimes accompanied by strings and winds.

sentences.zh: 郊廟宴饗亦用之。

translations.literal: Suburban rites, temple sacrifices, and feasts also used them.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifices, temple rites, and banquets also employed them.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，詔太樂、總章、鼓吹增修雜伎，造五兵、角觝、麒麟、鳳皇、仙人、長蛇、白象、白虎及諸畏獸、魚龍、辟邪、鹿馬仙車、高絙百尺、長趫、緣橦、跳丸、五案以備百戲。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, an edict ordered the Grand Music, Zongzhang, and Drum-and-Pipe offices to expand and repair miscellaneous entertainments, creating the Five Weapons, horn-butting, qilin, phoenix, immortals, long serpent, white elephant, white tiger, and various fearful beasts, fish and dragon, ward-off-evil, deer-horse immortal carriage, hundred-foot high rope, long stilts, pole-climbing, ball-juggling, and five-table acts to complete the hundred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, an edict ordered the Grand Music, Zongzhang, and Drum-and-Pipe offices to expand and repair miscellaneous entertainments, creating acts of the Five Weapons, horn-butting, qilin, phoenix, immortals, long serpent, white elephant, white tiger, and various fearsome beasts, fish and dragon, ward-off-evil, deer-horse immortal carriage, hundred-foot high rope, long stilts, pole-climbing, ball-juggling, and five-table displays to complete the hundred entertainments.

sentences.zh: 大饗設之於殿庭，如漢晉之舊也。

translations.literal: At grand feasts they were set up in the palace courtyard, as in the old practice of Han and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At grand feasts they were set up in the palace courtyard, following the old practice of Han and Jin.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，又增修之，撰合大曲，更為鍾鼓之節。

translations.literal: In the early reign of Emperor Taizong, they were further expanded and repaired; grand suites were composed and the bell-and-drum rhythms were renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early reign of Emperor Taizong, they were further expanded and repaired; grand suites were composed and the bell-and-drum rhythms were revised.

sentences.zh: 世祖破赫連昌，獲古雅樂，及平涼州，得其伶人、器服，並擇而存之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu defeated Helian Chang and obtained ancient elegant music; when Liang province was pacified, he obtained its performers, instruments, and costumes, and selected and preserved them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu defeated Helian Chang and obtained ancient court music; when Liang province was pacified, he acquired its performers, instruments, and costumes, selecting and preserving the best.

sentences.zh: 後通西域，又以悅般國鼓舞設於樂署。

translations.literal: Later, when the Western Regions were opened, the dances and drums of the Yueban kingdom were also established in the music office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Western Regions were opened, the dances and drums of the Yueban kingdom were also installed in the music bureau.

sentences.zh: 高宗、顯祖無所改作。

translations.literal: Emperors Gaozong and Xianzu made no changes or creations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Gaozong and Xianzu made no alterations or new creations.

sentences.zh: 諸帝意在經營，不以聲律為務，古樂音制，罕復傳習，舊工更盡，聲曲多亡。

translations.literal: The emperors' intent was on statecraft and they did not make pitch and rhythm their concern; ancient musical pitch systems were rarely transmitted and practiced; old craftsmen passed away one after another, and many songs and melodies were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperors focused on statecraft and did not make pitch and rhythm a priority; ancient musical systems were rarely transmitted; veteran craftsmen died off one after another, and many songs and melodies were lost.

sentences.zh: 太和初，高祖垂心雅古，務正音聲。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era, Emperor Gaozu devoted himself to elegant antiquity and strove to correct sounds and pitches.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe era, Emperor Gaozu devoted himself to elegant antiquity and strove to restore correct pitch and tone.

sentences.zh: 時司樂上書，典章有闕，[4]求集中祕羣官議定其事，并訪吏民，有能體解古樂者，與之修廣器數，甄立名品，以諧八音。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of Music submitted a memorial that the regulations were deficient,[4] requesting that officials of the central secretariat be assembled to deliberate and settle the matter, and also that officials and commoners be consulted—whoever could comprehend ancient music would join in expanding and repairing the number of instruments, selecting and establishing categories of names, to harmonize the eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Director of Music submitted a memorial noting deficiencies in the regulations,[4] requesting that officials of the central secretariat be assembled to deliberate and settle the matter, and that officials and commoners be consulted as well—whoever could comprehend ancient music would join in expanding and repairing the instrument inventory, selecting and establishing proper categories, to harmonize the eight kinds of sound.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 雖經眾議，於時卒無洞曉聲律者，樂部不能立，其事彌缺。

translations.literal: Although many deliberated, at the time there was ultimately no one who thoroughly understood pitch and rhythm; the music bureau could not be established, and the matter grew ever more deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Although many deliberated, at the time there was ultimately no one who thoroughly understood pitch and rhythm; the music bureau could not be established, and the deficiency grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 然方樂之制及四夷歌舞，稍增列于太樂。

translations.literal: Yet the system of regional music and the songs and dances of the four barbarians were gradually added to the Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Yet regional music and the songs and dances of the four outer peoples were gradually added to the Grand Music repertoire.

sentences.zh: 金石羽旄之飾，為壯麗於往時矣。

translations.literal: The adornments of metal, stone, feathers, and banners became more magnificent than in former times.
translations.idiomatic: The adornments of bells, stone chimes, feathers, and banners became more magnificent than ever before.

sentences.zh: 五年，文明太后、高祖並為歌章，戒勸上下，皆宣之管絃。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Empress Dowager Wenming and Emperor Gaozu both composed song texts to admonish and encourage high and low, and all were disseminated through pipes and strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Empress Dowager Wenming and Emperor Gaozu both composed song texts to admonish and encourage high and low, and all were disseminated through pipes and strings.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，中書監高允奏樂府歌詞，陳國家王業符瑞及祖宗德美，又隨時歌謠，不準古舊，辨雅、鄭也。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, Gao Yun, Director of the Secretariat, submitted the song texts of the Music Bureau, setting forth the state's royal enterprise, auspicious omens, and the virtue and excellence of the ancestors, and also the occasional songs and ballads, not conforming to ancient models, distinguishing ya from zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year, Gao Yun, Director of the Secretariat, submitted the song texts of the Music Bureau, setting forth the state's royal enterprise, auspicious omens, and the virtue and excellence of the ancestors, together with occasional songs and ballads that did not conform to ancient models, distinguishing proper court music from popular music.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，文明太后令曰：「先王作樂，所以和風改俗，非雅曲正聲不宜庭奏。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, Empress Dowager Wenming ordered: "The former kings made music to harmonize the winds and transform customs; music that is not elegant melody and correct sound should not be performed in court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, Empress Dowager Wenming ordered: "The former kings made music to harmonize the winds and transform customs; music that is not elegant melody and correct sound should not be performed at court.

sentences.zh: 可集新舊樂章，參探音律，除去新聲不典之曲，裨增鍾縣鏗鏘之韻。」

translations.literal: Collect old and new musical chapters, investigate and probe pitch and rhythm, remove new sounds and uncanonical melodies, and add to the resounding tones of the bell-chime."
translations.idiomatic: Collect old and new musical chapters, investigate pitch and rhythm, remove new sounds and uncanonical melodies, and enhance the resounding tones of the bell-chime ensemble."

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，高祖詔曰：「樂者所以動天地，感神祇，調陰陽，通人鬼。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year, Emperor Gaozu proclaimed: "Music is that by which heaven and earth are moved, spirits are stirred, yin and yang are harmonized, and humans and ghosts are connected.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year, Emperor Gaozu proclaimed: "Music is that which moves heaven and earth, stirs the spirits, harmonizes yin and yang, and connects the living with the dead.

sentences.zh: 故能關山川之風，以播德於無外。

translations.literal: Therefore it can relate to the winds of mountains and rivers and spread virtue to the boundless beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it can resonate with the winds of mountains and rivers and spread virtue to the farthest reaches.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，治用大矣。

translations.literal: Spoken from this perspective, its use in governance is great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, its importance to governance is immense.

sentences.zh: 逮乎末俗陵遲，正聲頓廢，多好鄭衞之音以悅耳目，故使樂章散缺，伶官失守。

translations.literal: When later customs declined, correct sounds were abruptly abandoned; many favored the sounds of Zheng and Wei to please the ears and eyes, and thus musical chapters were scattered and deficient, and court musicians lost their charge.
translations.idiomatic: When later customs declined, correct sounds were abruptly abandoned; many favored the licentious music of Zheng and Wei to please the ears and eyes, and thus musical chapters were scattered and incomplete, and court musicians lost their proper role.

sentences.zh: 今方釐革時弊，稽古復禮，庶令樂正雅頌，各得其宜。

translations.literal: Now we are reforming the defects of the age, examining antiquity and restoring ritual, hoping to make music correct the Ya and Song, each obtaining its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are reforming the defects of the age, examining antiquity and restoring ritual, hoping to make music restore the Ya and Song, each to its proper place.

sentences.zh: 今置樂官，實須任職，不得仍令濫吹也。」

translations.literal: In establishing music officials now, they must truly fulfill their duties and must not continue to be allowed to blow indiscriminately."
translations.idiomatic: In establishing music officials now, they must truly fulfill their duties and must not continue to be allowed to perform indiscriminately."

sentences.zh: 遂簡置焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon selections were made and appointments established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon selections were made and appointments established.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，又詔曰：「禮樂之道，自古所先，故聖王作樂以和中，制禮以防外。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, another edict proclaimed: "The way of ritual and music has been foremost since antiquity; therefore the sage kings made music to harmonize the inner, and fashioned ritual to guard against the outer.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year, another edict proclaimed: "The way of ritual and music has been foremost since antiquity; therefore the sage kings made music to harmonize the inner self and fashioned ritual to guard against external disorder.

sentences.zh: 然音聲之用，其致遠矣，所以通感人神，移風易俗。

translations.literal: Yet the use of sound and pitch reaches far indeed—it connects and moves humans and spirits, transforms the winds and changes customs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the power of sound and pitch reaches far indeed—it connects and moves humans and spirits, transforms the winds of custom and changes popular habits.

sentences.zh: 至乃簫韶九奏，鳳皇來儀；

translations.literal: So much so that when the Shaoshao was played nine times, the phoenix came to pay homage;
translations.idiomatic: So much so that when the Shaoshao was performed nine times, the phoenix came to pay homage;

sentences.zh: 擊石拊石，百獸率舞。

translations.literal: when stone chimes were struck and tapped, the hundred beasts led the dance.
translations.idiomatic: when stone chimes were struck and tapped, the hundred beasts led the dance.

sentences.zh: 有周之季，斯道崩缺，故夫子忘味於聞韶，正樂於返魯。

translations.literal: In the late Zhou, this way collapsed and was deficient; therefore the Master forgot flavor upon hearing the Shao, and corrected music upon returning to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhou, this tradition collapsed; therefore the Master forgot the taste of meat upon hearing the Shao, and restored correct music upon returning to Lu.

sentences.zh: 逮漢魏之間，樂章復闕，然博採音韻，粗有篇條。

translations.literal: By the Han and Wei period, musical chapters were again deficient, yet broadly collecting pitch and rhyme, there were roughly some chapters and articles.
translations.idiomatic: By the Han and Wei period, musical chapters were again incomplete, yet through broad collection of pitch and rhyme, there were roughly some written records.

sentences.zh: 自魏室之興，太祖之世尊崇古式，舊典無墜。

translations.literal: Since the rise of the Wei house, in the founding emperor's era ancient forms were honored and old regulations were not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rise of the Wei dynasty, in the founding emperor's era ancient forms were honored and old regulations were preserved.

sentences.zh: 但干戈仍用，文教未淳，故令司樂失治定之雅音，習不典之繁曲。

translations.literal: But weapons of war were still in use and literary culture was not yet pure; therefore the Director of Music lost the elegant sounds of settled governance and practiced uncanonical elaborate melodies.
translations.idiomatic: But warfare continued and literary culture was not yet refined; therefore the Director of Music lost the elegant sounds of settled governance and practiced uncanonical elaborate melodies.

sentences.zh: 比太樂奏其職司，求與中書參議。

translations.literal: Recently the Grand Music presented its official duties and requested joint deliberation with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Grand Music presented its official duties and requested joint deliberation with the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 覽其所請，愧感兼懷。

translations.literal: Reading their request, I feel both shame and gratitude together.
translations.idiomatic: Reading their request, I feel both shame and gratitude together.

sentences.zh: 然心喪在躬，未忍聞此。

translations.literal: Yet mourning fills my person, and I cannot bear to hear this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am still in mourning and cannot bear to hear such matters.

sentences.zh: [5]但禮樂事大，乃為化之本，自非通博之才，莫能措意。

translations.literal: [5] Yet ritual and music are great affairs, the root of transformation; unless one possesses comprehensive and broad talent, none can give them proper thought.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Yet ritual and music are weighty matters, the foundation of civilization; only someone of comprehensive and broad talent can give them proper consideration.

sentences.zh: 中書監高閭器識詳富，志量明允，每間陳奏樂典，頗體音律，可令與太樂詳採古今，以備茲典。

translations.literal: Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat, is richly endowed in talent and insight, with clear and trustworthy resolve; whenever he occasionally submitted memorials on musical regulations, he showed considerable understanding of pitch and rhythm—he may be ordered together with the Grand Music to thoroughly collect from antiquity and the present to complete this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat, is richly endowed in talent and insight, with clear and trustworthy resolve; whenever he submitted memorials on musical regulations, he showed considerable understanding of pitch and rhythm—he should be ordered together with the Grand Music to thoroughly survey antiquity and the present and complete this canon.

sentences.zh: 其內外有堪此用者，任其參議也。」

translations.literal: Whoever within or without is capable of this task, allow them to join in deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever within or outside the court is capable of this task may join in the deliberation."

sentences.zh: 閭歷年考度，粗以成立，遇遷洛不及精盡，未得施行。

translations.literal: Lu investigated and measured over several years and roughly completed the work, but when the capital was moved to Luoyang he had no time to refine it fully, and it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Lu investigated and measured over several years and roughly completed the work, but the move of the capital to Luoyang left no time to refine it fully, and it was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 尋屬高祖崩，未幾，閭卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Gaozu passed away, and before long Lu also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Gaozu passed away, and before long Lu died as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，閭引給事中公孫崇共考音律，景明中，崇乃上言樂事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu had enlisted Attendant-in-Ordinary Gongsun Chong to jointly investigate pitch and rhythm; in the Jingming era, Chong submitted a memorial on music affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu had enlisted Attendant-in-Ordinary Gongsun Chong to jointly investigate pitch and rhythm; during the Jingming era, Chong submitted a memorial on music affairs.

sentences.zh: 正始元年秋，詔曰：「太樂令公孫崇更調金石，燮理音準，其書二卷并表悉付尚書。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Zhengshi, an edict proclaimed: "Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong has readjusted metal and stone instruments and harmonized pitch standards; his two scrolls of writing together with his memorial are all to be delivered to the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Zhengshi, an edict proclaimed: "Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong has readjusted bells and stone chimes and harmonized pitch standards; his two scrolls of writing together with his memorial are all to be delivered to the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 夫禮樂之事，有國所重，可依其請，八座已下、四門博士以上此月下旬集太樂署，考論同異，博採古今，以成一代之典也。」

translations.literal: Ritual and music are what a state holds in esteem; his request may be followed—officials from the Eight Seats downward and Erudites of the Four Gates upward shall assemble at the Grand Music Office before the end of this month to examine and debate agreements and differences, broadly collecting from antiquity and the present, to complete the canon of a generation."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music are what a state holds in esteem; his request may be granted—officials from the Eight Seats downward and Erudites of the Four Gates upward shall assemble at the Grand Music Office before the end of this month to examine and debate agreements and differences, broadly surveying antiquity and the present, to complete the canon of an age."

sentences.zh: 十月，尚書李崇奏：「前被旨敕，以兼太樂令公孫崇更調金石，并其書表付外考試，登依旨敕以去。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Chong of the Ministry submitted: "Previously we received the imperial command that Acting Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong readjust metal and stone instruments, and that his writings and memorial be delivered for external examination; Deng proceeded according to the command and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Li Chong of the Ministry submitted: "Previously we received the imperial command that Acting Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong readjust bells and stone chimes, and that his writings and memorial be delivered for external examination; Deng proceeded according to the command.

sentences.zh: 八月初，詣署集議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the eighth month, we went to the office and assembled for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the eighth month, we went to the office and assembled for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 但六樂該深，五聲妙遠。

translations.literal: But the six kinds of music are profound in scope, and the five tones are subtle and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: But the six kinds of music are profound in scope, and the five tones are subtle and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 至如仲尼淵識，故將忘味；

translations.literal: As for Confucius, with his profound understanding, he was about to forget flavor;
translations.idiomatic: As for Confucius, with his profound understanding, he forgot the taste of meat;

sentences.zh: 吳札善聽，方可論辨。

translations.literal: Wu Zha, skilled in listening, alone could discuss and distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zha, skilled in listening, alone could discuss and distinguish.

sentences.zh: 自斯已降，莫有詳之。

translations.literal: From that time downward, none has examined it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, none has examined it in detail.

sentences.zh: 今既草創，悉不窮解，雖微有詰論，略無究悉。

translations.literal: Now that it is newly drafted, none fully comprehend it; although there were slight questions and debates, there was scarcely any thorough understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Now that it is newly drafted, none fully comprehends it; although there were slight questions and debates, there was scarcely any thorough understanding.

sentences.zh: 方欲商搉淫濫，作範將來，寧容聊爾一試，便垂竹帛。

translations.literal: We are just about to discuss excess and laxity and establish models for the future—how can we casually try it once and immediately inscribe it on bamboo and silk?
translations.idiomatic: We are just about to discuss excess and laxity and establish models for the future—how can we casually try it once and immediately commit it to written record?

sentences.zh: 今請依前所召之官并博聞通學之士更申一集，考其中否，研窮音律，辨括權衡。

translations.literal: We now request that according to the officials previously summoned, together with broadly learned scholars of comprehensive knowledge, another assembly be convened to examine what is correct and what is not, exhaustively investigate pitch and rhythm, and distinguish and summarize weights and measures.
translations.idiomatic: We now request that the officials previously summoned, together with broadly learned scholars of comprehensive knowledge, assemble again to examine what is correct and what is not, exhaustively investigate pitch and rhythm, and distinguish and summarize weights and measures.

sentences.zh: 若可施用，別以聞請。」

translations.literal: If it can be applied, we shall report separately and request approval."
translations.idiomatic: If it can be applied, we shall report separately and request approval."

sentences.zh: 制「可」。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript replied: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript replied: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 時亦未能考定也。

translations.literal: At the time they were also unable to examine and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were also unable to examine and fix it.

sentences.zh: 四年春，公孫崇復表言：「伏惟皇魏龍躍鳳舉，配天光宅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Gongsun Chong again submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that the august Wei, like a dragon leaping and a phoenix rising, matches heaven and dwells in glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, Gongsun Chong again submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that the august Wei, like a dragon leaping and a phoenix rising, matches heaven and dwells in glory.

sentences.zh: 世祖太武皇帝革靜荒嵎，廓寧宇內，兇醜尚繁，戎軒仍動，制禮作樂，致有闕如。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, Emperor Taiwu, pacified the wild frontier and brought peace throughout the realm; though fierce enemies still abounded and the war chariot still moved, the establishment of ritual and creation of music remained deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, Emperor Taiwu, pacified the wild frontier and brought peace throughout the realm; though fierce enemies still abounded and the war chariot still moved, the establishment of ritual and creation of music remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝德鍾後仁之期，道協先天之日，顧雲門以興言，感簫韶而忘味。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Xiaowen, accumulated virtue at the time of later benevolence and harmonized with the way of the prior heaven; gazing at Yunmen he was moved to speak, and feeling the Shaoshao he forgot flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Xiaowen, accumulated virtue at the time of later benevolence and harmonized with the way of the prior heaven; gazing upon Yunmen he was moved to speak, and upon hearing the Shaoshao he forgot the taste of meat.

sentences.zh: 以故中書監高閭博識明敏，文思優洽，紹蹤成均，實允所寄。

translations.literal: Therefore Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat, with broad knowledge and keen intelligence, literary thought excellent and harmonious, continuing the traces of Chengjun, was truly worthy of this trust.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat, with broad knowledge and keen intelligence, literary thought excellent and harmonious, continuing the tradition of Chengjun, was truly worthy of this trust.

sentences.zh: 乃命閭廣程儒林，究論古樂，依據六經，參諸國志，錯綜陰陽，以制聲律。

translations.literal: He then ordered Lu to broadly engage the forest of scholars, exhaustively discuss ancient music, rely on the Six Classics, consult the various state records, and interweave yin and yang to establish pitch and rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Lu to broadly engage the forest of scholars, exhaustively discuss ancient music, rely on the Six Classics, consult the various state records, and interweave yin and yang to establish pitch and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 鍾石管絃，略以完具，八音聲韻，事別粗舉。

translations.literal: Bells, stone chimes, pipes, and strings were roughly complete; the sounds and pitches of the eight tones were separately outlined in rough form.
translations.idiomatic: Bells, stone chimes, pipes, and strings were roughly complete; the sounds and pitches of the eight tones were separately outlined in rough form.

sentences.zh: 值遷邑崧瀍，未獲周密，五權五量，竟不就果。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Song and Chan, thorough completion was not achieved; the five weights and five measures ultimately did not reach fruition.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved to Song and Chan, thorough completion was not achieved; the five weights and five measures ultimately did not reach fruition.

sentences.zh: 自爾迄今，率多褫落，金石虛懸，宮商未會。

translations.literal: From then until now, most have been lost and fallen away; metal and stone hang empty, and gong and shang do not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, most have been lost; bells and stone chimes hang unused, and tonic and second do not harmonize.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下至聖承天，纂戎鴻烈，以金石未協，詔臣緝理。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, supremely sage, succeeding heaven, inheriting the great enterprise, because metal and stone were not harmonized, ordered me to put them in order.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, supremely sage, succeeding heaven and inheriting the great enterprise, because bells and stone chimes were not harmonized, ordered me to put them in order.

sentences.zh: 謹即廣搜秬黍，選其中形，又採梁山之竹，更裁律呂，制磬造鍾，依律並就。

translations.literal: I respectfully then broadly searched for black millet and selected the best specimens; I also gathered bamboo from Liang Mountain, recut the pitch pipes, fashioned stone chimes and cast bells, and completed all according to pitch.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully then broadly searched for black millet and selected the best specimens; I also gathered bamboo from Liang Mountain, recut the pitch pipes, fashioned stone chimes and cast bells, and completed all according to pitch.

sentences.zh: 但權量差謬，其來久矣，頃蒙付并州民王顯進所獻古銅權，稽之古範，考以今制，鍾律準度，與權參合。

translations.literal: But weights and measures have been erroneous for a long time; recently I was entrusted with the ancient bronze weight presented by Wang Xian of Bing province, checked it against ancient models, compared it with present standards, and found that bell pitch, rhythm, and measure all accord with the weight.
translations.idiomatic: But weights and measures have been erroneous for a long time; recently I was entrusted with the ancient bronze weight presented by Wang Xian of Bing province, checked it against ancient models, compared it with present standards, and found that bell pitch, rhythm, and measure all accord with the weight.

sentences.zh: 昔造猶新，始創若舊，異世同符，如合規矩。

translations.literal: What was made in the past seems new; what was first created seems old—different ages share the same token, as if fitting compass and square.
translations.idiomatic: What was made in the past seems new; what was first created seems old—different ages share the same standard, as if fitting compass and square.

sentences.zh: 樂府先正聲有王夏、肆夏、登歌、鹿鳴之屬六十餘韻，又有文始、五行、勺舞。

translations.literal: In the Music Bureau, the correct sounds of old include Wangxia, Sixia, dengge, Luming, and the like—more than sixty melodies—and also the Wenshi, Wuxing, and Shao dances.
translations.idiomatic: In the Music Bureau, the correct sounds of old include Wangxia, Sixia, dengge, Luming, and the like—more than sixty melodies—and also the Wenshi, Wuxing, and Shao dances.

sentences.zh: [6]太祖初興，置皇始之舞，復有吳夷、東夷、西戎之舞。

translations.literal: [6] When the founding emperor first rose, he established the Huangshi dance, and there were also dances of Wu Yi, Dong Yi, and Xi Rong.
translations.idiomatic: [6] When the founding emperor first rose, he established the Huangshi dance, and there were also dances of Wu Yi, Dong Yi, and Xi Rong.

sentences.zh: 樂府之內，有此七舞。

translations.literal: Within the Music Bureau, there are these seven dances.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Music Bureau, there are these seven dances.

sentences.zh: 太和初，郊廟但用文始、五行、皇始三舞而已。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era, suburban rites and temples used only the Wenshi, Wuxing, and Huangshi three dances.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe era, suburban sacrifices and temples used only the Wenshi, Wuxing, and Huangshi three dances.

sentences.zh: [7]竊惟周之文武，頌聲不同；

translations.literal: [7] I privately consider that in Zhou, Wen and Wu had different eulogy songs;
translations.idiomatic: [7] I privately consider that in Zhou, Wen and Wu had different eulogy songs;

sentences.zh: 漢之祖宗，廟樂又別。

translations.literal: in Han, the ancestral temple music of the founders was again distinct.
translations.idiomatic: in Han, the ancestral temple music of the founders was again distinct.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇魏四祖、三宗，道邁隆周，功超鴻漢，頌聲廟樂，宜有表章，或文或武，以旌功德。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the four ancestors and three founders of the august Wei, their way surpassing flourishing Zhou and their achievement exceeding great Han, should have eulogy songs and temple music manifest in written form, whether literary or martial, to display merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the four ancestors and three founders of the august Wei, their way surpassing flourishing Zhou and their achievement exceeding great Han, should have eulogy songs and temple music set forth in written form, whether literary or martial, to display merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 自非懿望茂親、雅量淵遠、博識洽聞者其孰能識其得失。

translations.literal: Unless one is of excellent reputation and eminent kinship, elegant breadth and profound distance, broad knowledge and comprehensive hearing—who else can discern its gains and losses?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one is of excellent reputation and eminent kinship, elegant breadth and profound insight, broad knowledge and comprehensive learning—who else can discern its gains and losses?

sentences.zh: 衞軍將軍、尚書右僕射臣高肇器度淹雅，神賞入微，徽讚大猷，聲光海內，[8]宜委之監就，以成皇代典謨之美。

translations.literal: Your servant Gao Zhao, General of the Guard and Vice Director of the Left Ministry, is of refined breadth and elegance, with divine appreciation reaching into the subtle, praising the great design, his fame shining throughout the realm,[8] and should be entrusted to supervise and complete it, to achieve the beauty of the august dynasty's canon and plan.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Gao Zhao, General of the Guard and Vice Director of the Left Ministry, is of refined breadth and elegance, with divine appreciation reaching into the subtle, praising the great design, his fame shining throughout the realm,[8] and should be entrusted to supervise and complete it, to achieve the beauty of the august dynasty's canon and plan.

sentences.zh: 昔晉中書監荀勗前代名賢，受命成均，委以樂務，崇述舊章，儀刑古典，事光前載，豈遠乎哉。

translations.literal: Formerly Xun Xu, Director of the Secretariat of Jin, a renowned worthy of a prior age, received the mandate at Chengjun and was entrusted with music affairs, honoring and expounding old regulations and taking classical antiquity as model—his achievement illuminated prior records; is this not close at hand?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Xun Xu, Director of the Secretariat of Jin, a renowned worthy of a prior age, received the mandate at Chengjun and was entrusted with music affairs, honoring and expounding old regulations and taking classical antiquity as model—his achievement illuminated prior records; is this not a close precedent?

sentences.zh: 又先帝明詔，內外儒林亦任高閭申請。

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor's clear edict also entrusted Gao Lu to submit requests from the forest of scholars within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor's clear edict also entrusted Gao Lu to submit requests from the forest of scholars within and without.

sentences.zh: 今之所須，求依前比。」

translations.literal: What is needed now, I request, should follow the prior precedent."
translations.idiomatic: What is needed now, I request, should follow the prior precedent."

sentences.zh: 世宗知肇非才，詔曰：「王者功成治定，制禮作樂，以宣風化，以通明神，理萬品，贊陰陽，光功德，治之大本，所宜詳之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong knew Zhao lacked talent and proclaimed: "When a king's achievement is complete and governance settled, he establishes ritual and creates music to spread customs and transform, to illuminate and connect with spirits, to order the myriad categories, to assist yin and yang, and to glorify merit and virtue—this is the great foundation of governance and should be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong knew Zhao lacked talent and proclaimed: "When a king's achievement is complete and governance settled, he establishes ritual and creates music to spread customs and transformation, to illuminate and connect with spirits, to order the myriad categories, to assist yin and yang, and to glorify merit and virtue—this is the great foundation of governance and should be examined in detail.

sentences.zh: 可令太常卿劉芳亦與主之。」

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang may also be ordered to jointly direct it."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Fang may also be ordered to jointly direct it."

sentences.zh: 永平二年秋，尚書令高肇，尚書僕射、清河王懌等奏言：「案太樂令公孫崇所造八音之器并五度五量，太常卿劉芳及朝之儒學，執諸經傳，考辨合否，尺寸度數悉與周禮不同。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Yongping, Gao Zhao, Director of the Ministry, and Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, Vice Director of the Ministry, and others submitted: "We find that the eight kinds of instruments and the five measures and five weights made by Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong, when Liu Fang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, and the Confucian scholars of the court held to the various classics and commentaries and examined whether they accorded, all differed from the Rites of Zhou in dimensions and measurements.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Yongping, Gao Zhao, Director of the Ministry, and Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, Vice Director of the Ministry, and others submitted: "We find that the eight kinds of instruments and the five measures and five weights made by Grand Music Director Gongsun Chong, when Liu Fang, Grand Master of Ceremonies, and the Confucian scholars of the court held to the various classics and commentaries and examined whether they accorded, all differed from the Rites of Zhou in dimensions and measurements.

sentences.zh: 問其所以，稱必依經文，聲則不協，以情增減，殊無準據。

translations.literal: When asked the reason, they said they must follow the classic text, but the sounds did not harmonize, and increases and decreases were made according to inclination, with no standard basis whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: When asked the reason, they said they must follow the classic text, but the sounds did not harmonize, and increases and decreases were made according to inclination, with no standard basis whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 竊惟樂者皇朝治定之盛事，光贊祖宗之茂功，垂之後王。

translations.literal: I privately consider that music is the great achievement of the dynasty's settled governance, glorifying and praising the abundant merit of the ancestors, to be handed down to later kings.
translations.idiomatic: I privately consider that music is the great achievement of the dynasty's settled governance, glorifying and praising the abundant merit of the ancestors, to be handed down to later kings.

sentences.zh: 不刊之制，宜憲章先聖，詳依經史。

translations.literal: An unalterable system should take the former sages as constitutional model and follow the classics and histories in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An unalterable system should take the former sages as constitutional model and follow the classics and histories in detail.

sentences.zh: 且二漢、魏、晉歷諸儒哲，未聞器度依經，而聲調差謬。

translations.literal: Moreover, through the Two Han, Wei, and Jin, among all the Confucian sages, we have never heard of instruments and measures following the classics while the pitch and tone were erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, through the Two Han, Wei, and Jin, among all the Confucian sages, we have never heard of instruments and measures following the classics while the pitch and tone were erroneous.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，請使臣芳準依周禮更造樂器，事訖之後，集議並呈，從其善者。」

translations.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate and request that your servant Fang be ordered to remake the musical instruments strictly according to the Rites of Zhou; when the task is complete, assemble for deliberation and present together, adopting what is best."
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers jointly deliberate and request that your servant Fang be ordered to remake the musical instruments strictly according to the Rites of Zhou; when the task is complete, assemble for deliberation and present together, adopting what is best."

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 芳上尚書言：「調樂諧音，[9]本非所曉，且國之大事，亦不可決於數人。

translations.literal: Fang submitted to the Ministry saying: "Harmonizing music and pitch[9] is not what I originally understood, and moreover a great affair of state cannot be decided by a few people.
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted to the Ministry saying: "Harmonizing music and pitch[9] is not what I originally understood, and moreover a great affair of state cannot be decided by a few people.

sentences.zh: 今請更集朝彥，眾辨是非，明取典據。

translations.literal: I now request that court luminaries be assembled again, that the multitude distinguish right from wrong, and that canonical evidence be clearly taken.
translations.idiomatic: I now request that court luminaries be assembled again, that the multitude distinguish right from wrong, and that canonical evidence be clearly taken.

sentences.zh: 資決元凱，然後營制。」

translations.literal: Relying on the judgment of the wise, then construct and establish."
translations.idiomatic: Relying on the judgment of the wise, then construct and establish."

sentences.zh: 肇及尚書邢巒等奏許，詔「可」。

translations.literal: Zhao and Xing Luan of the Ministry and others submitted approval, and an edict replied: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Xing Luan of the Ministry and others submitted approval, and an edict replied: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 於是芳主修營。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fang took charge of construction and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fang took charge of construction and repair.

sentences.zh: 時揚州民張陽子、義陽民兒鳳鳴、陳孝孫、戴當千、吳殿、陳文顯、陳成等七人頗解雅樂正聲，八佾、文武二舞、鐘聲、管絃、登歌聲調，芳皆請令教習，參取是非。

translations.literal: At the time seven men—Zhang Yangzi of Yang province, Er Fengming, Chen Xiaosun, Dai Dangqian, Wu Dian, Chen Wenxian, and Chen Cheng of Yiyang—understood elegant music and correct sounds rather well; Fang requested that they all be ordered to teach and practice the eight rows, the Wen and Wu two dances, bell sounds, pipes and strings, and dengge pitch, and to join in determining right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time seven men—Zhang Yangzi of Yang province, Er Fengming, Chen Xiaosun, Dai Dangqian, Wu Dian, Chen Wenxian, and Chen Cheng of Yiyang—understood elegant music and correct sounds rather well; Fang requested that they all be ordered to teach and practice the eight rows, the Wen and Wu two dances, bell sounds, pipes and strings, and dengge pitch, and to join in determining right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 永平三年冬，芳上言：「觀古帝王，罔不據功象德而制舞名及諸樂章，今欲教文武二舞，施之郊廟，請參制二舞之名。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yongping, Fang submitted: "Observing the ancient emperors and kings, none failed to base dance names and various musical chapters on merit and symbolize virtue; now wishing to teach the Wen and Wu two dances and apply them at suburban rites and temples, I request that names for the two dances be jointly established.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Yongping, Fang submitted: "Observing the ancient emperors and kings, none failed to base dance names and various musical chapters on merit and symbolize virtue; now wishing to teach the Wen and Wu two dances and apply them at suburban sacrifices and temples, I request that names for the two dances be jointly established.

sentences.zh: 竊觀漢魏已來，鼓吹之曲亦不相緣，今亦須制新曲，以揚皇家之德美。」

translations.literal: I privately observe that from Han and Wei onward, the drum-and-pipe melodies have also not been connected in sequence; now new melodies must also be created to spread the virtue and excellence of the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: I privately observe that from Han and Wei onward, the drum-and-pipe melodies have also not been connected in sequence; now new melodies must also be created to spread the virtue and excellence of the royal house."

sentences.zh: 詔芳與侍中崔光、郭祚，黃門游肇、孫惠蔚等四人參定舞名并鼓吹諸曲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fang together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, and Yellow Gate You Zhao and Sun Huiwei—the four of them—to jointly fix the dance names and the various drum-and-pipe melodies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Fang together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, and Yellow Gate You Zhao and Sun Huiwei—the four of them—to jointly fix the dance names and the various drum-and-pipe melodies.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，[10]芳又上言：「臣聞樂者，感物移風，諷氓變俗，先王所以教化黎元，湯武所以〔改章功德。

translations.literal: That winter,[10] Fang again submitted: "I have heard that music moves things and transforms the winds, admonishes the people and changes customs—the means by which former kings civilized the common folk, and by which Tang and Wu therefore reformed regulations and proclaimed merit where the source text is defective before this phrase.
translations.idiomatic: That winter,[10] Fang again submitted: "I have heard that music moves things and transforms the winds, admonishes the people and changes customs—the means by which former kings civilized the common folk, and by which Tang and Wu therefore reformed regulations and proclaimed merit where the source text is defective before this phrase.

sentences.zh: [11]晉氏失政，中原紛蕩。

translations.literal: [11] The Jin house lost proper governance, and the Central Plains were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: [11] The Jin house lost proper governance, and the Central Plains were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 劉石以一時姦雄，跋扈魏趙；

translations.literal: Liu and Shi, as momentary treacherous heroes, domineered over Wei and Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Liu and Shi, as momentary treacherous heroes, domineered over Wei and Zhao;

sentences.zh: 苻姚以部帥強豪，趦趄關輔。

translations.literal: Fu and Yao, as tribal chieftains and powerful magnates, hesitated and faltered in the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Yao, as tribal chieftains and powerful magnates, hesitated and faltered in the Guanxi region.

sentences.zh: 於是禮壞樂隳，廢而莫理。

translations.literal: Thereupon ritual collapsed and music was ruined, abandoned and left unreformed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon ritual collapsed and music was ruined, abandoned and left unreformed.

sentences.zh: 大魏應期啟運，奄有萬方，雖日不暇給，常以禮樂為先。

translations.literal: Great Wei responded to the age and opened its destiny, suddenly possessing the myriad regions; though days allowed no rest, ritual and music were always placed first.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei responded to the age and opened its destiny, suddenly possessing the myriad regions; though days allowed no rest, ritual and music were always placed first.

sentences.zh: 古樂虧闕，詢求靡所，故頃年以來，創造非一，考之經史，每乖典制。

translations.literal: Ancient music was deficient and incomplete, and inquiry found nowhere to seek it; therefore in recent years creations have been more than one, but when examined against the classics and histories, each departs from canonical regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient music was deficient and incomplete, and inquiry found nowhere to seek it; therefore in recent years creations have been numerous, but when examined against the classics and histories, each departs from canonical regulation.

sentences.zh: 遂使鏗鏘之禮，未備於郊廟；

translations.literal: Thus the resounding rites were not complete at suburban sacrifices and temples;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the resounding rites were not complete at suburban sacrifices and temples;

sentences.zh: 鼓舞之式，尚闕於庭陛。

translations.literal: the forms of drum and dance were still lacking in the courtyard and steps.
translations.idiomatic: the forms of drum and dance were still lacking in the courtyard and steps.

sentences.zh: 臣忝官宗伯，禮樂是司，所以仰慚俯愧，不遑寧處者矣。

translations.literal: I, unworthy, hold the office of Minister of Rites, in charge of ritual and music—therefore looking up I feel shame and looking down I feel guilt, with no leisure for peace.
translations.idiomatic: I, unworthy, hold the office of Minister of Rites, in charge of ritual and music—therefore looking up I feel shame and looking down I feel guilt, with no leisure for peace.

sentences.zh: 自獻春被旨，賜令博採經傳，更制金石，并教文武二舞及登歌、鼓吹諸曲。

translations.literal: Since receiving the command in the spring of submission, I was granted orders to broadly collect from classics and commentaries, remake metal and stone instruments, and also teach the Wen and Wu two dances and the dengge and drum-and-pipe melodies.
translations.idiomatic: Since receiving the command in the spring of submission, I was granted orders to broadly collect from classics and commentaries, remake bells and stone chimes, and also teach the Wen and Wu two dances and the dengge and drum-and-pipe melodies.

sentences.zh: 今始校就，謹依前敕，延集公卿并一時儒彥討論終始，莫之能異。

translations.literal: Now the proofreading is complete; respectfully following the prior command, I assembled the nobles and ministers together with the Confucian luminaries of the time to discuss from beginning to end, and none could differ.
translations.idiomatic: Now the proofreading is complete; respectfully following the prior command, I assembled the nobles and ministers together with the Confucian luminaries of the time to discuss from beginning to end, and none could differ.

sentences.zh: 謹以申聞，請與舊者參呈。

translations.literal: I respectfully report this and request that it be presented together with the old version for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully report this and request that it be presented together with the old version for comparison.

sentences.zh: 若臣等所營形合古制，擊拊會節，元日大饗，則須陳列。

translations.literal: If what we your ministers have constructed accords with ancient regulation in form, and striking and beating meet the rhythm, then at the New Year's grand feast it must be arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: If what we your ministers have constructed accords with ancient regulation in form, and striking and beating meet the rhythm, then at the New Year's grand feast it must be arrayed.

sentences.zh: 既歲聿云暮，三朝無遠，請共本曹尚書及郎中部率呈試。

translations.literal: Since the year is already ending and the three audiences are not far off, I request that together with the Director and section chiefs of this ministry we lead the presentation for trial performance.
translations.idiomatic: Since the year is already ending and the three audiences are not far off, I request that together with the Director and section chiefs of this ministry we lead the presentation for trial performance.

sentences.zh: 如蒙允許，賜垂敕判。」

translations.literal: If graciously permitted, grant your command for judgment."
translations.idiomatic: If graciously permitted, grant your command for judgment."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「舞可用新，餘且仍舊。」

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed: "The dances may use the new versions; the rest for now remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "The dances may use the new versions; the rest for now remain as before."

sentences.zh: 鼓吹雜曲遂寢焉。〕

translations.literal: The drum-and-pipe miscellaneous melodies were thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The drum-and-pipe miscellaneous melodies were thereupon shelved.

sentences.zh: 〔初，御史中尉元匡與芳等競論鍾律。

translations.literal: At first, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang competed with Fang and others in debating bell pitch and rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang competed with Fang and others in debating bell pitch and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 孝明帝熙平二年冬，[12]匡復上言其事，太師、高陽王雍等奏停之。〕

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiping under Emperor Xiaoming,[12] Kuang again submitted a memorial on the matter, and Grand Preceptor Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, and others submitted to halt it.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xiping under Emperor Xiaoming,[12] Kuang again submitted a memorial on the matter, and Grand Preceptor Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, and others submitted to halt it.

sentences.zh: 先是，有陳仲儒者自江南歸國，頗閑樂事，請依京房，立準以調八音。

translations.literal: Earlier, there was one Chen Zhongru who returned from the south and was quite versed in music affairs; he requested to follow Jing Fang and establish pitch standards to tune the eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, there was one Chen Zhongru who returned from the south and was quite versed in music affairs; he requested to follow Jing Fang and establish pitch standards to tune the eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年夏，有司問狀。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Shengui, the relevant offices inquired into his credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Shengui, the relevant offices inquired into his credentials.

sentences.zh: 仲儒言：

translations.literal: Zhongru said:
translations.idiomatic: Zhongru said:

sentences.zh: 前被符，問：「京房準定六十之律，後雖有器存，[13]曉之者尠。

translations.literal: Previously I received a command asking: "Jing Fang's pitch standard fixed the sixty pitch pipes; though instruments survived afterward,[13] those who understood them were few.
translations.idiomatic: Previously I received a command asking: "Jing Fang's pitch standard fixed the sixty pitch pipes; though instruments survived afterward,[13] those who understood them were few.

sentences.zh: 至熹平末，張光等猶不能定絃之急緩，聲之清濁。

translations.literal: By the end of Xiping, Zhang Guang and others still could not fix the tightness and looseness of strings or the clarity and muddiness of sounds.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Xiping, Zhang Guang and others still could not fix the tightness and looseness of strings or the clarity and muddiness of sounds.

sentences.zh: 仲儒授自何師，出何典籍而云能曉？」

translations.literal: From what teacher did Zhongru receive instruction, from what classic or record does he claim understanding?"
translations.idiomatic: From what teacher did Zhongru receive instruction, from what classic or record does he claim understanding?"

sentences.zh: 但仲儒在江左之日，頗愛琴，又嘗覽司馬彪所撰續漢書，[14]見京房準術，成數昞然，而張光等不能定。

translations.literal: But when Zhongru was in the lands south of the Yangtze, he was quite fond of the qin, and once read the Continuation of the Book of Han compiled by Sima Biao,[14] where he saw Jing Fang's pitch-standard technique with its numbers clearly set forth, while Zhang Guang and others could not fix it.
translations.idiomatic: But when Zhongru was in the lands south of the Yangtze, he was quite fond of the zither, and once read the Continuation of the Book of Han compiled by Sima Biao,[14] where he saw Jing Fang's pitch-standard technique with its numbers clearly set forth, while Zhang Guang and others could not fix it.

sentences.zh: 仲儒不量庸昧，竊有意焉。
